additions.reason: The 'good point' is the essential positive quality within every person that redeems them and constitutes their spiritual worth. It is the foundation of self-judgment toward merit (דין לכף זכות). The Rebbe explicitly calls it a bechina concept — it is the inner dimension of the chasid.
additions.source_quote: בִּבְחִינַת הַנְּקֻדָּה טוֹבָה הַזֹּאת הוּא בְּחִינַת חָסִיד

additions.reason: Being a chasid is explicitly stated to be the bechina of the nekuda tova — the outer expression of the inner good point. David's self-praise 'guard my soul for I am a chasid' is interpreted as applying to any person in the dimension of their nekuda tova. Both concepts belong to the same essential nature: the domain of positive spiritual identity.
additions.source_quote: בִּבְחִינַת הַנְּקֻדָּה טוֹבָה הַזֹּאת הוּא בְּחִינַת חָסִיד

bechina_pairs_found_in_source_text.source_quote: בִּבְחִינַת הַנְּקֻדָּה טוֹבָה הַזֹּאת הוּא בְּחִינַת חָסִיד
bechina_pairs_found_in_source_text.note: Double bechina language — the text uses both 'בִּבְחִינַת' and 'הוּא בְּחִינַת' in the same sentence, explicitly equating these two concepts.

narrative_concepts_not_bechina.note: Saying Tehillim — the main topic and practice. Discussed in eitza (prescriptive) terms, not bechina. It is what one does, not a parallel-nature equation.

War against the evil inclination — the referent of David's battles. Described causally: David's wars in Psalms = one's personal war against the yetzer. This is a metaphorical interpretation (eitza), not a bechina equation.
Judging oneself favorably — an act/practice prescribed by the teaching. It is the eitza that leads to finding the nekuda tova, not a bechina parallel.
Elevating one's heart in the ways of God (from the verse about Yehoshafat). Cited as proof for the principle of lifting oneself up in Divine service. Narrative/prooftext, not a bechina statement.
